limitations: The 'tissue enriched' category is defined by the Human Protein Atlas as ≥4-fold higher expression in the named tissue versus any other tissue; it is an RNA-level annotation and does not guarantee protein-level specificity.
The favourable-prognosis share uses only the 'validated prognostic favorable' category from the TCGA prognostics column; genes annotated as 'potential prognostic favorable' are not counted.
The heatmap displays the 15 highest-expressed genes per cohort in their own tissue; expression in the other two tissues is shown for context but those genes are not necessarily enriched there.
The grouped bar chart plots median nTPM on the same axis as the two shares (0–1 proportions); the different scales make direct visual comparison of the three series difficult.

limitations: The 'tissue enriched' category in the Human Protein Atlas is defined by RNA expression (≥4-fold higher in the tissue of interest vs any other tissue); it does not guarantee protein-level enrichment.
The favourable-prognosis share uses only the 'validated prognostic favorable' category from the TCGA prognostics column; genes annotated as 'potential prognostic favorable' are not counted.

The heatmap displays the 15 highest-expressed genes per cohort in their own tissue; these may not be the 15 highest in the other two tissues, so cross-tissue comparisons within the heatmap are limited to this selected subset.

The grouped bar chart plots mean_is_blood, mean_is_favorable, and median_nTPM on the same axis; because median_nTPM is on a very different scale (hundreds to thousands) than the two shares (0–1), the bar for median_nTPM dominates visually.
